questions.stem: A shape is translated by the vector $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$. What happens to each point?
questions.explanation: In the column vector $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$, the top number gives the horizontal movement (positive = right) and the bottom number gives the vertical movement (negative = down). So each point moves 3 right and 2 down.

questions.stem: A point $P(1, 4)$ is translated by $\begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$. What are the coordinates of the image $P'$?
questions.explanation: Add the vector components to the coordinates: $x' = 1 + (-5) = -4$ and $y' = 4 + 3 = 7$. So $P' = (-4, 7)$.

questions.stem: Which property is always preserved under a translation?

options.text: The orientation and size of the shape
Only the area but not the side lengths

questions.explanation: A translation slides every point of a shape by the same amount in the same direction. The shape keeps its size, angles, and orientation. Only the position changes.
